newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar sees slow start after holiday.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar sees slow start after holiday.

text.p: White sugar futures got off to a slow start on Tuesday morning with minimal volume trading before the open of the New York market.
Light commission house crossing of October/December was reported at $2.00 and the nearby August/October spread was broadly unchanged, bid at $9.00.
At 1045 GMT August was the only contract to have posted any price movement after the close on Friday, London's last session after the extended holiday break.
August was down 50 cents at $313.40 and the overall volume of 160 lots was broadly split between the three nearby months.
Technical analysts said August's recent reaction low of $308.30 represented immediate support and a bullish stance could be adopted while this level held. Nearby resistance was pegged at $317.50.
In physical news, market sources said Pakistan bought one cargo of white sugar at the end of last week at $351.00 a tonne although details of the supplier and the shipment period have yet to emerge.

Pakistan also said it would decide on Wednesday the result of a tender to buy 50,000 tonnes of crystal whites, to reach Karachi in two equal shipments by June 20 and July 10. The tender was opened on Saturday.
In Paris just 32 lots of the spot August contract were on the board. The position stood 40 cents firmer at $312.90.
